en: The Bhikṣu Saṃghavarman, desiring to enter nirvāṇa,
preached the Sūtra of the Six Perfections and addressed the good sons and good daughters within Jambudvīpa: "Since my birth in Jambudvīpa,
I have acted as a Great Compassionate Father to teach and transform sentient beings, wandering through the world from time immemorial."
Throughout kalpas of vast duration, he has manifested billions of emanations to rescue and deliver sentient beings; yet,
seeing that the beings of Jambudvīpa have committed many evil deeds, [he acts accordingly].
They do not believe in the Buddha-dharma,
and those who engage in evil deeds are many;
I cannot bear to witness this.
My body shall immediately enter nirvana;
my relics and images will be spread throughout Jambudvīpa to guide and transform sentient beings.
In the future, when the world of the Semblance Dharma has reached its full extent and the True Dharma flourishes,
I and the Honored Buddha Maitreya shall descend together to be born in this world,
sitting side by side in the City of Transformation.
The Savior of Auspicious Conditions originally resided in his own abode,
located in the Eastern Sea.
This was due to the conditions for a pure land in past lives;
because sentient beings were stubborn, ignorant, and difficult to transform,
they did not believe in the Buddha-dharma.
They have committed many evil deeds.
I have departed from my original place and traveled to the Western Land to teach and transform sentient beings;
there I am known as Śākyamuni Buddha.
The Eastern Land was subsequently overwhelmed by five hundred venomous dragons and submerged into a great ocean.
All sentient beings sank within the sea and were transformed into turtles, crocodiles, fish, and tortoises.
After my passing, I shall return from the land of the Hu in the west to be reborn in Jambudvīpa,
to rescue and deliver those with virtuous affinities,
and to preserve the seeds of Buddha-nature.
I see that the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa are everywhere in their realms violent and malevolent,
devouring one another.
He is incorrigible.
I shall now enter parinirvāṇa.
As for my śarīra, my original bones, I wish for them to remain in Sizhou hereafter.
If there are good men or good women who,
with a compassionate heart and filial piety,
revere my image, observe the long fast, and subsist on vegetarian food.
Those who keep my name in mind are scattered throughout Jambudvīpa;
I take pity on them as they witness the evil age in which armies of force arise in competition.
All manner of evils shall oppress your body, leaving you without autonomy.
Later, when I descend with the Honored Buddha Maitreya to be born in our native land,
my feet shall tread upon the waters of the sea until they are dried up.
Consequently, the various devas, nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of holy beings established themselves at the center of the Eastern Sea,
where they constructed a city of transformation with walls made of gold and silver.
The ground shall be made of lapis lazuli,
and the palaces shall be made of the seven treasures;
I shall later arrive in Jambudvīpa.
In transmitting the Buddha-dharma,
he transmitted only this sutra to edify those with virtuous affinities.
The six classes of disciples returned to me;
through the transformation city, they were spared from Jambudvīpa and,
having endured all their hardships, attained complete peace and security.
Food and clothing are provided spontaneously;
one shall eternally receive ultimate bliss.
The celestial Māras and heterodox paths are separated by the Weak Water.
It will not come to cause harm.
I shall deliver six kinds of people. The first to be delivered is one who is filial and obedient toward their parents and reveres the Triple Gem. The second to be delivered is...
Not killing sentient beings is the third precept.
Not drinking alcohol or eating meat is the fourth precept.
Maintaining an impartial and benevolent heart and refraining from theft is the fifth precept.
Practicing the ascetic dhūta austerities, he delighted in repairing bridges and performing various meritorious deeds. As for the sixth perfection:
he took pity on the poor and was mindful of the sick.
They bestowed clothing and food,
providing ultimate relief to the destitute and helpless;
such were these people who followed the six perfections of the virtuous path.
I previously sent a hundred youths to lead the superior jewel-ship across the Weak Water so that they might avoid drowning and reach the City of Transformation;
had it not been for my people who have practiced the Six Perfections, this would not have been possible.
If one sees this sutra of mine and does not believe or accept it, thereby slandering the True Dharma,
you should know that this person’s roots of evil from past lives will result in physical retribution;
they shall either encounter thieves, soldiers, or pestilence and die.
Some may be burned or swept away by water and fire;
others may suffer from seasonal epidemics or malignant diseases, or encounter officials and fall into prison.
Sentient beings who do not cultivate goodness all undergo immeasurable suffering and affliction.
Upon death, they enter hell with no time of release;
for ten thousand kalpas, they shall not return to the human realm.
Good sons and good daughters who transcribe this sutra and,
with resolute intent, accept and uphold it.
If you encounter the waters of the kalpa of destruction, the fires of the kalpa of destruction, black winds, or the darkness of heaven,
I shall therefore illuminate you with immeasurable light.
Through these causes and conditions, you shall together arrive at the Buddha-land.
All return together to the City of Nirvāṇa and fully attain liberation.
Namo saṃghāya | Namo saṃghakṣitāya | Svāhā | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Balaye | Svāhā. The Saṃghāvaśeṣa Sūtra.
